# Deviload 2.7.8

Devil Music gets a calmer workspace, cover-colored Ambient lighting, lyrics alongside browsing, a compact mini-player and a QR phone remote.

## What changed

- **A connected music workspace:** larger search, resizable library and Now Playing panels, compact music cards, clearer action buttons and a vinyl playback animation. Navigation and long tab labels remain readable at smaller window sizes.
- **Ambient throughout the app:** cover colors soften the background, sidebar, header and player. Light reacts to the playing audio, with a stronger effect around the playback controls. The existing logo receives a slow pearlescent shimmer. Reduced-motion settings disable the decorative movement.
- **Six themes:** Ambient, Light Liquid Glass, Matte black, Black Liquid Glass, Midnight and Studio green. Ambient is the default for new profiles and replaces Classic; saved choices of the other themes remain intact. Glass effects are inside the app, not native desktop transparency.
- **Lyrics in two places:** open the full player or flip the Now Playing cover into lyrics without leaving your library. Both use the same playback clock, scrolling and highlighting. Click a timed line to seek, adjust text size or return to the current line after scrolling.
- **A compact mini-player:** opening it hides the main window. Return to Devil Music or close the mini-player to restore the main window. Previous/next, play/pause, repeat, shuffle, seek and volume stay available, with a rotating vinyl cover and matching theme.
- **Phone music remote:** click the remote icon and scan its QR code on the same Wi-Fi. Playback, seeking, volume, repeat and shuffle follow the desktop, as do the theme and interface language. Sound stays on the computer. It uses a separate local connection from file transfer and needs no account or hosted service.
- **Clearer update notes:** What's new opens automatically once for each installed version and remains available from its button.

## What was fixed

- Search focus, side-panel sizing, tab wrapping and the layout of inline lyrics in narrow windows.
- Timeline fill and volume controls no longer visually lag behind their sliders.
- Switching to the mini-player no longer leaves both windows visible.
- The full player's header can move the window on Windows and macOS without interfering with its return button.
- Discovery no longer inserts regional chart shelves. Local listening, likes, exclusions and personal mixes still shape recommendations; search remains available for any artist or region.
- The reported WebKit renderer workaround now applies automatically before window creation on Debian 13 GNOME/Wayland, including normal `.deb` launches. Explicit renderer overrides take precedence. Other Linux configurations keep their existing behavior; no forced switch to X11 is added.

## Availability and limits

- Word highlighting depends on the lyrics record containing actual word timings. Otherwise the player uses timed lines or plain text. An instrumental label is shown only when the source identifies the track as instrumental; missing lyrics receive a separate message.
- The remote uses HTTP on a trusted local network. Allow private-network access if the firewall asks. Turning it off revokes the link; unused sessions expire after 30 minutes. It is a controller, not shared listening or phone audio streaming.
- The Debian 13 GNOME/Wayland workaround is based on the reporter's successful manual launch. Testing this build on that affected machine, including resizing and window buttons, is still pending. See [Linux compatibility](https://github.com/Pronexsteam/deviload/blob/main/docs/linux-renderer-compatibility.md).
- macOS remains an unsigned, unnotarized test build. Updater signatures are separate from Windows Authenticode and Apple notarization.

The application identity, profile paths and signed updater endpoints are unchanged. Local music and download data are preserved when updating normally.
